questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I wanted to go to an English speaking country, so I could master my English skills. 

I also tried to aim for a larger university, so I was sure that I would be able to meet other exchange students.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fine. However I used the email for exchange students a lot, and got quick responses to almost everything.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a orientation where you could meet other exchange students and hear about the university, courses etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
Shared rooms
Single rooms

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: As I shared a room with another student - and therefore had no acces to a kitchen - it was required that I had a meal plan. I could choose between a bronze, silver and gold meal plan. Meal plan options was restaurants, fast food and cafeterias.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend living off campus, if you get a shared dorm room. You have to share a small room with another person, and share bathroom with 10 others. And it was very expensive when the meal plan also is a requirement.

I wouldn't recommend students to live at Vanier.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I missed the date of the opening of the course registration, and all the interestering courses said something around 'no spaces, extra spaces might be available'. I contacted the apartment of Political Science and they gave me acces to 3/4 courses after a few minutes!!

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The proces is first come, first served, so it is important that you are ready. You are able to change the courses until two weeks during the semester.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I reached out to my department, and they helped a lot

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I wasn't really, because I missed the day where the courses was made public. However I found some that was still open

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be ready on the date where course registrations are made public

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took 4000 level courses which is four year courses. It made sense since I was at my fourth year of university (first year of MA)

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: My classes were mainly discussion forums, where my professor asked some questions, and then the students had to discuss for three hours. That was very different from UCPH

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Political culture of race and racism 
Economic Unions and Globalization
Protest movements and democracy
Contemporary EU Politics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Political culture of race and racism gave me a lot of knowledge and was very good at challenging biases
Contemporary EU Politics was made as 'Model UN', where you had to discuss EU law. Very intersting way to learn

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: No one.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Eating out is 15 pct cheaper than in DK

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Nice gym

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
They had a gym where you could train for a very nice price 
I know that they also hosted some cultural events, but I didn't participate

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The gym was great

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
I did a lot of sightseeing in Toronto, where I both saw all the main sights but also tried to get out in some less famous areas
I watched a lot of live sport, e.g hockey, basketball and baseball which was so cool.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I think it was easy. Everybody was very nice

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I had some classes where the same students participated in both. I think that helped a lot

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not any

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really liked how diverse Toronto is. People come from all over the world, and have so many interspersing perspectives on things!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be aware of strikes..... There was a strike going on for 2 month of my stay, and some of my classes got cancelled. Apparently it was something that have happened 3 times the last 7 years. I was very stressed and I didn't feel like UCPH gave me the right support.
2. Be ready on the day where the course portal open 
3. Dont live at campus, unless you get your own place!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Please follow how the strike situation is. Are the faculty members happy with their wage increase? maybe another strike won't happen again

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Get to know a lot of sweet people, and learn a lot about Canadian culture

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The strike was a huge challenge for me mentally. I was very stressed about wether I could receive a grade and return with ECTS points

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
